domain: Enterprise Zero-Trust SASE & FIDO2 Workforce Identity
title: $4.8M Global Zero-Trust SASE and FIDO2 Workforce Rollout for Meridian Financial
executive_summary: Acme CyberShield proposes a $4.8M three-year deal to replace Meridian Financial's legacy VPN with Zero-Trust SASE and FIDO2 passwordless authentication for 12,500 employees. Technical review reveals critical gaps between sales SLA and latency promises and engineering limits on availability, biometrics, and offline support.

proposal_document.title: Commercial Proposal v1.0
proposal_document.text: Acme CyberShield proposes deployment for 12,500 workforce identities across 14 global sites with 99.99% authentication availability SLA, including FIDO2 passwordless login with biometric step-up authentication completing in under 2 seconds for 99% of attempts. All SASE edge traffic will be inspected with sub-15ms added latency globally, and continuous posture evaluation will re-assess device trust every 60 seconds without user friction. We guarantee zero additional hardware required as all biometric verification uses native device authenticators, with full support for offline FIDO2 authentication for remote field staff for up to 30 days. Deployment will complete in 21 days with zero downtime migration from legacy VPN, including 24/7 dedicated SOC support and $500,000 service credit backing for any SLA breach.

technical_specification.title: Technical Architecture Spec v4.2
technical_specification.text: The platform is architected for 10,000 concurrent FIDO2 sessions per region with 99.9% authentication service availability excluding scheduled maintenance windows every Sunday 02:00-04:00 UTC. Biometric step-up authentication requires server-side verification with p95 completion in 4.8 seconds, and continuous posture evaluation re-assesses device trust every 60 seconds via lightweight agent telemetry. SASE PoPs add 35-60ms inspection latency depending on region and TLS decryption policy, with offline authentication limited to cached TOTP fallback for maximum 24 hours requiring prior online enrollment. Migration from legacy VPN/IPsec requires a 4-hour cutover window per site and supports up to 12,500 provisioned identities with additional license tier required beyond 10,000 concurrent sessions.

commitments.claim: 99.99% authentication availability SLA with no exclusions
commitments.spec_quote: 99.9% authentication service availability excluding scheduled maintenance windows every Sunday 02:00-04:00 UTC
commitments.explanation: Proposal promises four-nines availability while spec commits only to three-nines and explicitly excludes weekly 2-hour maintenance windows, making the SLA mathematically unachievable as stated.

commitments.claim: Offline FIDO2 authentication for remote field staff for up to 30 days
commitments.proposal_quote: full support for offline FIDO2 authentication for remote field staff for up to 30 days
commitments.explanation: Spec provides no support for offline FIDO2; it only allows cached TOTP fallback for maximum 24 hours requiring prior online enrollment, leaving the 30-day FIDO2 claim entirely without technical basis.

commitments.claim: Zero additional hardware as all biometric verification uses native device authenticators
commitments.proposal_quote: zero additional hardware required as all biometric verification uses native device authenticators
commitments.spec_quote: Biometric step-up authentication requires server-side verification with p95 completion in 4.8 seconds
commitments.explanation: Spec confirms server-side verification is required but does not define supported native authenticator matrix, TPM versions, or server HSM capacity, so it is unclear whether legacy devices and regulated sites truly need no additional hardware.

commitments.claim: Continuous posture evaluation re-assessing device trust every 60 seconds
commitments.proposal_quote: continuous posture evaluation will re-assess device trust every 60 seconds without user friction
commitments.spec_quote: continuous posture evaluation re-assesses device trust every 60 seconds via lightweight agent telemetry
commitments.explanation: Spec explicitly confirms the same 60-second re-assessment interval via agent telemetry, directly supporting the proposal's continuous evaluation cadence claim.
